messages:
Mark (Acme Corp): Hey team — weird MFA/session thing after migrating to a new phone. I deleted the old device from Okta, re-enrolled MFA, then when users sign in they briefly hit the app but subsequent API calls get 401. The login flow returns 200 on /auth/callback but our UI then gets bounced by /api/v1/session/validate with body 'session_assertion_mismatch'. Cookie shows rw_session present (SameSite=None; Secure).

Jen (Support): ugh, that sounds bad. Is this OIDC or SAML? Which browser and did you try private mode? Also can you paste a redacted request + full 401 body? Any recent org/domain config changes?

Mark (Acme Corp): OIDC via Okta. Steps I did: removed old device, re-enrolled on new phone, then SSO login + accepted device trust. Chrome 117 macOS. Incognito same behavior. Network dump (redacted):

```curl 'https://api.redwood.ai/api/v1/session/validate' \
  -H 'Cookie: rw_session=REDACTED' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'\n\n# response\n# 401 {"error":"session_assertion_mismatch","detail":"device-trust-token not found for assertion"}
```

Jen (Support): thanks — looping in @Max and @Lee to check runtime/auth side. Max, Lee: customer reports session assertion mismatch after device re-enroll. Cookie present but validation fails. Could be device-trust token rotation or cookie-binding change.

DeployBot: deploy completed: eng-runtime/chore/session-cookie-samesite-adjust at 2026-02-28T14:15:43Z :rocket:

Max (SRE): pulling logs for org acme-prod-12. Do you have an approximate time for the failures? Want to match traces around the deploy.

Mark (Acme Corp): started seeing it ~2026-02-28T14:22:00Z and persisted.

Max (SRE): I see the failed validates in edge logs — trace id trc_0a9c7... linked here: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trc_0a9c7

Lee (Eng-Sec): quick hypothesis: the recent change altered cookie binding/validation ordering. If the IdP issues a new device assertion while the old cookie still references the prior binding, the server will reject the assertion even though login completed. Also the SameSite tweak could cause the callback to set cookies inconsistently across flows.

Max (SRE): repro I'm running in staging: 1) sign-in via SSO callback -> set rw_session cookie -> POST /api/v1/session/validate (OK). 2) simulate device re-enroll / purge old token -> repeat validate -> 401 session_assertion_mismatch. So we can reproduce.

Jen (Support): for customers: short-term ask them to clear cookies and fully re-login. If multiple users affected, we can run a targeted server-side session invalidation for the org so everyone gets fresh assertions.

Mark (Acme Corp): clearing cookies helped for me initially but another user still had the flip. Can you run the invalidation for org acme-prod-12? Prefer server-side to avoid hitting SRE every time someone swaps phones.

Lee (Eng-Sec): propose mitigation: run an org-scoped browser-session invalidation (do not touch API keys). Also add a guard in the callback so if we detect stale assertion cookies we force re-auth instead of setting a bad cookie. Finally, add an alert on spikes of session_assertion_mismatch.

Max (SRE): running targeted invalidation now with internal tool: 

```# internal admin tool
redwood-admin sessions invalidate --org acme-prod-12 --scope browser_sessions --reason "mfa-device-reenroll-session-assertion-mismatch"
```
SessionBot: [automated] invalidation job queued (job_id: job_9998) — est completion 30s

SessionBot: [automated] invalidation job completed (job_id: job_9998) — 218 sessions expired

Max (SRE): done. Users will have to re-run the full SSO flow and re-accept device trust. Mark, can you verify?

Mark (Acme Corp): confirmed — users re-logged in and so far stable. Thanks for the quick action.

Jen (Support): I'll email a recap and keep the ticket open for 24h to monitor stability. Also, Mark — would you like a short user-facing blurb we can share to reduce support noise?

Mark (Acme Corp): yes please — something simple about re-logging after enrolling a new device.

Max (SRE): suggested user-facing guidance to share: 
- After enrolling a new MFA device, sign out of the browser and sign back in (or clear cookies for app.redwood.ai) to refresh session bindings.
- If you see repeated sign-in prompts, include the 401 response body and your approximate time and we will trace it.

Lee (Eng-Sec): follow-ups we will own: add assertion-staleness detection to callback to redirect to re-auth, instrument a metric for session_assertion_mismatch with org dim, and audit cookie SameSite/domain behavior for callback flows.

Jen (Support): I'll follow up with a concise summary and link to the trace. Closing contingent on 24h stability check. :thumbsup:

Mark (Acme Corp): thanks again — will ping if anything else pops up.
